neighbours.label: a copular perception verb (feel, look, seem, sound) whose complement is an impression, predicting 'like' / 'as'
fire: She tried to cheer him up, but that didn't feel much better to him.
With all the cloud servers, the whole network starts to look like one big machine.
In the lab, the machines made what seemed like a click every few seconds.
The new album sounds like something recorded in a garage.
We kept passing each other on the track and it just felt comfortable.
From the hill, the city lights look like a field of stars.
The first practice of the season didn't feel that way for the coach.
His explanation seems a bit too simple to me.
quiet: She tried to cheer him up, but that didn't help much at all for him.
With all the cloud servers, the whole network starts to become one big machine.
In the lab, the machines made a loud click every few seconds.
The new album was recorded in a garage in two weeks.
We kept passing each other on the track and it just went on for hours.
From the hill, the city lights stretch across the whole valley.
The first practice of the season didn't start until noon for the coach.
His explanation is a bit too simple, in my opinion.

notes: Card: ' feel' x7, ' look' x5, ' looks' x4, ' feels' x3, ' seem' x3, ' sound' x3. The + pole peaks on the following ' as' / ' like'. Near misses keep the topic and replace the perception verb with become/help/be or rephrase without one.
